purpose: Preserve a falsifiable cross-domain analogy between JANUS-LAPIS repair-state resolution and the OdontoForge appositional-growth search architecture without promoting the analogy to a biological mechanism claim.
lapis_question: How long does a useful transient repair state persist before successful EXIT/resolution, and what separates recovery from pathological persistence?
odonto_question: How long does a partial search state persist before it crystallizes into a verified certificate, dies by contradiction, or regenerates into a new branch?

mapping.resolution_exit: verified terminal certificate or exact branch closure

candidate_transfer_test.name: TRANSIENT_STATE_EXIT_CLOCK
candidate_transfer_test.rule: Use the same abstract bookkeeping vocabulary across biological and computational lanes, then test each lane only with its own domain-valid measurements.
required_outputs: independent verification of the terminal state

epistemic_boundaries: OdontoForge does not establish a biological mechanism of wound repair.
A biological EXIT mechanism does not establish an algorithmic complexity result.
Similar state-machine geometry is an analogy until predictive transfer is demonstrated prospectively.
Any transferred hypothesis must be tested with domain-specific controls and independent evidence.

requires: predeclared shared metric before outcome inspection
at least one prospective prediction in each domain
no semantic promotion from visual similarity alone

relation_to_exit_clock: This bridge adds no new biological evidence. It supplies a computational control system in which transient-state lifetime, successful EXIT, conflict, and regeneration can be measured exactly and compared structurally with the biological EXIT CLOCK program.
